title: Corridor Mapping for Tigers
description: Using GPS collars and camera traps to map dispersal corridors between protected reserves in central India.
objectives: Identify functional tiger corridors between protected areas
Assess corridor connectivity and bottlenecks
Provide data for corridor conservation planning
methodology: GPS collar telemetry on resident tigers combined with camera trap grids across potential corridor habitats. Landscape genetic analysis to validate functional connectivity.

title: Anuran Diversity in Wetlands
description: Seasonal survey of amphibian species richness across restored urban wetlands.
objectives: Document anuran species composition in restored wetlands
Compare diversity metrics across restoration ages
Identify indicator species for wetland health
methodology: Visual encounter surveys and acoustic monitoring across 12 restored wetlands over 4 seasons. Comparison with reference natural wetlands.
findings: Restored wetlands show rapid colonization by common anuran species; specialist species require longer restoration periods and connectivity to source populations.

title: Beetle Microbiome Study
description: Characterising gut bacterial communities and their role in dung beetle digestion.
objectives: Sequence gut microbiome of dung beetle species
Identify bacterial taxa involved in plant fiber digestion
Compare microbiome across beetle diets
methodology: 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of gut contents from field-collected dung beetles. Metagenomic analysis for functional annotation.

title: Whole-Genome of Clownfish
description: Assembling and annotating a high-quality reference genome for anemonefish.
objectives: Generate chromosome-level genome assembly for Amphiprion ocellaris
Annotate genes involved in symbiosis and sex change
Provide resource for clownfish research community
methodology: PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing combined with Hi-C scaffolding. Gene annotation using RNA-seq from multiple tissues.
findings: High-quality genome assembly reveals expanded gene families related to immunity and chemical sensing. Candidate genes for sequential hermaphroditism identified.
notes: Migrated from projects.html. Lead researcher 'S. Patel' from source. Institution not specified. Species likely Amphiprion ocellaris based on assets.html - needs verification.

title: Fox Habitat Restoration
description: Reforestation of urban green belts to support resident red fox populations.
objectives: Restore native vegetation in urban green corridors
Monitor red fox population response
Reduce human-fox conflict through habitat improvement
methodology: Native tree/shrub planting in degraded urban green belts. Camera trap monitoring of fox activity. Community engagement for conflict mitigation.

location.region: Urban area, Japan (inferred from researcher name)

findings: Restored green corridors showed increased fox activity within 12 months. Human-fox conflict reports decreased in areas with restored habitat buffers.

title: Moth Pollination Networks
description: Molecular gut-content analysis of nectar-feeding moths and their host plants.
objectives: Identify plant species visited by nocturnal moths
Construct moth-plant pollination networks
Assess role of moths in plant reproductive success
methodology: DNA metabarcoding of moth proboscis/gut contents. Plant reference library for identification. Network analysis of bipartite interactions.
findings: Moths visit diverse plant species, including many not visited by diurnal pollinators. Network structure reveals high complementarity between nocturnal and diurnal pollinator guilds.
